paper.title: Comparative transcriptome analysis revealing dormant conidia and germination associated genes in Aspergillus species: an essential role for AtfA in conidial dormancy
paper.authors: Hagiwara D, Takahashi H, Kusuya Y, Kawamoto S, Kamei K, Gonoi T
paper.association_evidence: Methods: 'The RNA-sequencing read data was deposited to the DDBJ Sequence Read Archive under accession No. PRJDB4747' (Europe PMC full-text accession search).

study_summary.objective: Identify genes linked to conidial dormancy and early germination that are shared by A. fumigatus, A. niger and A. oryzae.
study_summary.experimental_design: For each species, hyphae (PDB, sub-stationary phase), dormant conidia (7-day PDA plates) and conidia incubated 1 h in PDB were compared; this BioProject holds the A. oryzae RIB40 libraries (one per stage, no replicates).
study_summary.main_finding: Dormant conidia were enriched for stress-protection transcripts (e.g. catalases) and 1-h conidia for ribosome/translation genes; in A. fumigatus the bZIP regulator AtfA was needed to keep the dormant-conidia program and repress germination genes.

tags.note: no germ tube or swelling yet at 1 h

notes: Single library per developmental stage (no biological replicates).
The paper's cross-species comparison also used A. fumigatus and A. niger data, which are not in this BioProject's atlas samples.
